featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Third Wave Coffee recently and it was a really good experience. They have a buy one get one free offer on Wednesdays, which is honestly a great deal and makes it worth planning a visit mid-week.

I tried the chocolate frappe and it was genuinely impressive. The texture was smooth and nicely thick, not icy or watered down like it sometimes is at other places. The chocolate flavor was rich without being too sweet, so it didn’t feel heavy even after a few sips.

What stood out the most was the quality. It just tasted better than what you usually get at bigger chains like Starbucks. It didn’t feel overly processed or rushed. There was more depth in the flavor, and you could tell a bit more care had gone into making it.

The place itself is also quite nice to sit in. It has a relaxed vibe, good for catching up with someone or just sitting with your drink for a while. Not too noisy, not too dull either.

Overall, really liked it. The Wednesday offer is a nice bonus, and the chocolate frappe alone makes it worth going back.

What made my visit especially memorable was Priyanka, one of their baristas. She was incredibly friendly, attentive, and clearly passionate about coffee. The service overall was smooth and efficient, even during a busy period, and the staff maintained a welcoming vibe throughout. Thanks to Priyanka’s excellent service and the café’s commitment to quality, Third Wave Coffee definitely stands out as a go-to place for coffee lovers.

featured_reviews.name: jeet sandhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
BFF Cafe on Marve Road, Malad West, is a delightful place that offers a warm and comfortable café experience. From the moment you enter, the café gives off a friendly and relaxed vibe, making it a great spot to unwind after a long day or spend some quality time with close friends. The interiors are simple yet pleasant, creating a cozy atmosphere that feels inviting and peaceful.

The food at BFF Cafe is definitely one of its highlights. The menu is well curated with a good variety of options, and the taste does not disappoint. Every dish is prepared fresh and served with care, reflecting good quality and attention to detail. The portion sizes are satisfying, and the flavors are well balanced, making it a great value for money. The beverages complement the food perfectly and are ideal for casual conversations and relaxed evenings.

Another aspect that stands out is the service. The staff is polite, courteous, and attentive, ensuring that customers feel comfortable throughout their visit. Orders are served on time, and the team is always ready to help with recommendations or special requests. This level of hospitality adds a personal touch that enhances the overall experience.

One important thing to note is that the café has a relatively small seating area. While this adds to its cozy charm, it may not be suitable for large groups, especially during busy hours. However, for solo visits, couples, or small groups, the space works perfectly and feels intimate rather than crowded.

Overall, BFF Cafe is a great choice if you’re looking for good food, pleasant ambiance, and friendly service in Malad West. It’s an ideal spot for casual meetups and relaxed dining, and definitely a place worth visiting again with friends.

featured_reviews.name: Noel Nadar
featured_reviews.review_text: I got to know about this place via Instagram reels. The reels fascinated me to go visit this place and try their food. It's located in Malad East, just opposite the Gol Garden at a walkable distance from the station. Undoubtedly it's a cool place with an unmatchable vibe, those walls stuck with posters, popular memes, song names etc etc. There are even books to read. There are high chairs to sit on as well as comfortable cushions to relax and have your food. The place is small and not very suitable for a large group of friends maybe. I was shocked to know that it's open till 3 am in the night! I've never known cafes being open till that late post midnight. The owner was friendly. The mocktails tasted okay. The entire menu is vegetarian and mostly jain. The music playing in the background was good. The hot coffee was really good. If you're a vegetarian foodie then you could visit this place someday and feel a little nostalgic looking at the walls. It'd call it a good hangout spot to visit with friends.

featured_reviews.name: Mehta Dimple
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌟 Dreamhouse Café – A Hidden Gem in Malad East! 🌟
📍 Near Gol Garden, Malad East

Visited this cozy little café recently and I’m still drooling over the taste! We tried Bubble Gum Mocktail, Mexican Nachos, Basil on the Rocks Pasta, Classic Veg Cheese Burger, Peri Peri Spicy Paneer Pizza, Jangal Me Mangal Panini, and their Brownie Milkshake – and let me tell you, every single item was bursting with flavor! 😍

The quality and taste are simply outstanding. The owner is extremely warm and welcoming, and the place is spotless clean.

Now coming to the ambience – it’s a walk down memory lane! Pure Bollywood + Old-school nostalgia vibes. You’ll spot vintage items like an old telephone, filmy posters, and so many quirky details. It’s hard to explain in words – you’ve got to visit and feel it for yourself. 💫

Though the café is small, they’ve managed the space so smartly that you don’t feel cramped at all. The ambience is unique, and it makes you want to just sit back and relax for hours.

And guess what? It’s a 100% Jain café! But honestly, even if you’re not Jain, the taste is so amazing that you won’t miss anything. It’s perfect for all foodies.

💰 Pricing is very reasonable for the quality and experience you get.

⭐ Final Verdict: 5/5 stars from me!
If you’re in or around Malad, this place is a must-visit. Great food, great vibes, and a heartwarming experience overall!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cococart is honestly that one place I keep going back to without even thinking twice. On days when I don’t feel like experimenting or figuring out somewhere new, this is my default spot—and it always feels just right.

The vibe is super cozy and comforting. They have these cute little cabins, books around you, and even small cabinets with chocolates from different parts of the world, which makes the place feel warm and a bit special. It’s perfect for just sitting with your laptop or catching up with friends.

I have to mention—their hot chocolate is one of the best. It’s my go-to here. Apart from that, I’ve tried their nachos, pasta, avocado toast, cheesy fries, and Burmese khao suey, and they’re all really good and satisfying.

The menu used to be bigger earlier, and now it feels a bit limited—especially for vegetarians—but whatever they do have is fresh, tasty, and feels wholesome.

Also, the staff is genuinely very friendly, which makes you want to come back. And the fact that they usually have some discount or offer going on just makes it even better.

It’s just one of those places that feels easy, familiar, and comforting every single time.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Located inside Oberoi Mall, Cococart & Cafe is a vibrant and spacious café that’s perfect for casual hangouts. The vibes are lively yet comfortable, making it a great spot to unwind, catch up with friends, or even spend some relaxed solo time.

The food quality is impressive, with a well-curated menu offering tasty bites and satisfying beverages. Whether you’re in for light snacks or indulgent treats, the taste and presentation both stand out.

One of the biggest advantages here is affordability—especially if you use platforms like District or EazyDiner. We booked through District and got a flat 50% discount, which made the overall experience extremely value-for-money.

The café is quite spacious compared to many mall cafés, so finding seating isn’t usually a hassle. It’s also quite popular among the younger crowd, which adds to the energetic and social atmosphere.

Overall, a great place for good food, great deals, and chill vibes right in the heart of Goregaon.

Subject: Serious Complaint Regarding Unprofessional and Unsafe Conduct at CCD Orlem

I am writing to formally raise a serious complaint regarding the behaviour of a barista named **Prakash** at **CCD Orlem**. My experience at this outlet was deeply uncomfortable, unprofessional, and concerning—especially as a woman visiting the café alone.

From the moment I entered, Prakash displayed a lack of basic etiquette and courtesy. He repeatedly pressured me to place an order immediately, creating an intimidating and uncomfortable environment rather than a welcoming one. At no point was his tone polite or respectful.

I raised a concern to another barista about people keeping their legs on the seating (again unhygienic), but that staff member was equally unprofessional and rude, responding angrily instead of addressing the issue, and then Prakash escalated the situation by calling his manager and making dismissive remarks about me, implying that I had “argued with other staff earlier,” which was misleading and untrue.

Unfortunately, when I spoke directly to the manager, his response was equally **arrogant and biased**, showing no interest in listening or resolving the issue. The overall attitude from both staff members was unprofessional and dismissive.

As a woman, I did not feel safe or respected in this environment. I eventually packed my belongings and left the café solely because of how uncomfortable and unwelcome I was made to feel.

This behaviour reflects very poorly on CCD Orlem and is damaging to the brand’s reputation. A café should be a safe, inclusive, and professional space—especially for solo patrons. Customers should not be made to feel pressured, judged, or disrespected simply for choosing to sit and work before ordering.
I found mosquitoes and cockroaches too in cafe and when called it out, request was taken casually. Many times Wifi doesn't work.

I strongly believe Prakash’s conduct needs to be reviewed and addressed seriously. If such behaviour continues unchecked, CCD Orlem risks losing loyal customers and its goodwill.

I request that this matter be investigated and appropriate action be taken to ensure professional conduct, customer safety, and basic courtesy at this outlet.

name: Bombay Coffee House Fort
description:
Bombay Coffee House is an elegant coffee shop that serves a variety of Coffees, Savories, Hot Meals & Breakfast all day as well as a fully functioning patisserie.

Bombay in the '70s was defined by the intermingling of various communities and sharing of the food from each one of these communities. Irani Kheema, Akuri on toast, the roadside Sev Puri, or even some of the legacies of the continental cuisine which the English introduced. We have incorporated these favorites At Bombay Coffee House along with the more recent favorites like The Hakka Noodle Bowl & Pastas. We want to bring back the old days of going to a coffee shop for wholesome freshly made comfort food and conversations over a cup of coffee.

featured_reviews.name: kalyani auti
featured_reviews.review_text: Very tasty food! We had Aubergine Teriyaki, Pepperoni Pizza, Fresh Lime Soda, Rosemary Fennel Lemonade and Chocolate Profiterole. The Aubergine Teriyaki is a must try! Amazing flavors with the nice texture of aubergine and black rice. The Rosemary Fennel Lemonade tasted amazing with it. The ambience is also good, nice jazz music. Good service as well.

featured_reviews.name: Suraj Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Kala Ghoda Cafe during the Kala Ghoda Festival with friends, and what a find this place turned out to be. Tucked away inside a small lane, it’s a little difficult to spot. After the madness of the fest, this café felt like a lake in a desert, felt calm, comforting, and exactly what we needed.
The vibe is warm and lively at the same time, with a charming setup and even a hidden bar counter that adds to the character of the place.
Coming to the food and drinks, they are the absolute winners. I tried the Masala Cappuccino, and it was truly unique, with a lovely kick of masala chai flavours blended into the coffee. Something I’ve never had before and surprisingly addictive.
The Cheese Chilli Toast, recommended by the waiter, did not disappoint—super cheesy with perfectly crispy bread. The Cottage Cheese Burger was honestly to die for, easily one of the best vegetarian burgers I’ve had—flavourful, filling, and perfectly balanced.
And the real star of the show was the Hash Brown dish “Rosti, crispy on the outside, creamy on the inside, and just cooked to perfection. Absolute comfort food.
Overall, great food, lovely coffee, welcoming vibes, and a peaceful break from the festival rush. Kala Ghoda Cafe is definitely a place I’d keep coming back to.

featured_reviews.name: Diya D'Sa
featured_reviews.review_text: Cozy ambiance and great service! The server recommended the chili cheese toast and it did not disappoint—perfectly crisp, cheesy, and with the right amount of spice. The waffle was good as well, though it came with quite a bit of nuts, granola, and raisins (great if you enjoy that). With the fresh fruit, I didn’t even need the syrup. My favorites were definitely the cheese toast and the chai. I also picked up a bag of their coffee beans, which are perfect for making coffee at home or even garnishing espresso martinis.

featured_reviews.name: Paras Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text: Kala Ghoda Café in Fort makes for a memorable stop. Service was decent, though it could be sharper. The food hit the right notes—the mushroom black rice risotto was warm and comforting, the four-cheese pizza hearty and fulfilling, and the carrot dish pleasantly fine. What truly elevates the experience is the café’s vibe and ambiance, which are simply noteworthy. Overall, a good outing worth revisiting!!!!!

featured_reviews.name: Anusuya
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Calm Vegetarian Haven in Kala Ghoda

Tucked away in the charming bylanes of the food area at Kala Ghoda Zen Cafe is a lovely vegetarian-only spot that offers a welcome break from the city's rush. The interiors are quaint with a warm relaxed vibe and the space is spread across two levels – a cosy ground floor and a quieter mezzanine level that’s perfect if you’re looking for a bit more privacy or calm.

The service is friendly and attentive which adds to the overall charm. The menu has plenty of interesting vegetarian options. We ordered the falafel wrap which was crunchy flavourful and left us wanting more. Light yet satisfying. The tomato pesto cheese sandwich was equally delicious – fresh and well made with comforting flavours.

And the cappuccino – really one of the highlights. Very very good. Smooth strong and creamy just the way a proper cappuccino should be.

Zen Cafe is the kind of place you’ll want to return to – for a peaceful solo break a quiet chat or simply to enjoy good food and coffee in a lovely tucked away corner of Kala Ghoda.

featured_reviews.name: SoulCranell
featured_reviews.review_text:
Atmosphere:
If I had to describe the vibe of Zen cafe it would be "cosy". The interiors make you feel really comfortable and you can just relax and enjoy your meal time with some magazines.

Food:
My orders were definitely not the typical "cafe order" since I had visited for lunch and was hungry, so I had to order a proper fulfilling meal. I had ordered, "Moroccan chickpea curry with rice" and I kid you not it was so delicious. It had that perfect home-cooked healthy meal vibe and to compliment it I had ordered fresh lime soda.

Service:
Since I had visited on a busy day, staff was very much occupied but still attentive. Overall 10/10 would recommend this place.

Tip: Make a prior reservation to save yourself from the hassle of waiting.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
“Zen Café, Colaba- where calm meets craft.
Tried their veggie sushi roll, croissant with hot chocolate, and couldn’t help but admire the cozy rustic vibe. The space feels effortlessly artistic — warm lights, wooden textures, and the aroma of fresh bakes wrapping you in peace. A perfect corner for slow mornings, deep thoughts, and good food that speaks less and feels more.”

featured_reviews.name: Sakshi Lawand
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away in the artsy lanes of Kala Ghoda, Zen Cafe is a quiet escape from the city's chaos, a minimalist, calming space perfect for slow mornings, work sessions, or thoughtful conversations. With natural light pouring in, wooden accents, and an almost meditative vibe, the ambiance lives up to the name “Zen.”

The menu leans towards healthy, vegetarian fare with Mediterranean and global influences. Their open sandwiches, hummus plates, and freshly baked goods are flavorful and light. Coffee is excellent, smooth and well-balanced, and the cold brews are especially worth a try. Portions are moderate, and presentation is clean and understated.

Prices are on the premium side, but you're paying for both quality and the peaceful setting, a rarity in South Mumbai. Service is polite and unhurried, which works well with the relaxed pace of the cafe.

A perfect spot to read, write, or simply slow down for a bit, Zen Cafe is a hidden gem for anyone who values good food in a beautiful, uncluttered space.

featured_reviews.name: Anupriya Karande
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of my most favourite cafés in the city & I always keep going back. It’s tucked in a quaint lane in Kalaghoda. Cozy vibes, sweet staff with great service & amazing food. Definitely try their platters, it’s value for money. My go-to order is always a Mocha with butter croissant 🥐☕️

featured_reviews.name: SRP
featured_reviews.review_text:
It was mid-morning and really wanted some caffeine. As usual the outside temperature was hot and quickly found this cafe that looked promising. As soon I went inside , I was pleasantly surprised with the incredible interior. Everything was nicely decorated, warm wood tones, cool temperature inside and great staff.

The menu first - so happy that menu is clearly labeled with all the allergens. As a vegan, this was pleasing. Don’t care if you have a couple items on the menu, but glad they are marked. Thank you.

Had a Dark Chocolate Affogato. First had the espresso a little bit and it was so good. So smooth with a little cream and with fruity tones. With ice cream, the espresso was divine.

Wish I could go Mumbai downtown more to have their other coffee offerings. Next time I am in Mumbai for sure.

featured_reviews.name: Sneha Lenze
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Nandan Coffee in Fort, Mumbai, and it turned out to be much more than just a coffee stop. Housed in a beautifully restored heritage building, the café offers a calm, elegant atmosphere that's perfect for slow mornings, reading, or catching up with friends. Their specialty coffee is sourced from their own organic estate in Kodaikanal, resulting in rich, well-balanced brews with distinct flavour profiles. The food complements the coffee well, and the overall experience feels thoughtfully curated. A great spot for coffee lovers who appreciate both quality brews and a charming ambience

featured_reviews.name: Megha Ghosh
featured_reviews.review_text: Love the location and the ambience. But I think somewhere cafés in Mumbai are focusing too much on presentation over substance. While the coffees were great the food is too expensive for the quantity and the taste. Most of the small plates are not a fit as accompaniment with coffee or matcha in my opinion the menu needs massive overhaul. The rosti tasted like alloo gobhi burnt sabzi and the tomato and onions on it don’t go with coffee or matcha. Eggs are not accompanied with breads so you order for eggs and separately for breads and avocados if you like! The bill was too high, and the food was below average. I expected so much better.

featured_reviews.review_text:

1) Iced Brown Butter Cookie Mocha
2) Mediterranean Spiced Eggs

4) Tiramisu French Toast
